answer: Each identity must prove a distinct network origin: one ASN and its /24 subnet, verified by reverse DNS and a BGP route authorization, with payouts capped per ASN. A lone honest user clears one check, while a sybil herd from one centre shares one cap, so its reward per fake falls like water down a canyon. Each extra fake needs another rented ASN and another signed ROA, so cost rises with every identity, not once per herd; a plume of forged records still fails the live BGP check. Proofs and caps sit on-chain, so any verifier replays each ROA, a record as hard to fake as jade is to carve.
